compatible.title: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
compatible.intro: Connect any server that speaks the OpenAI API — local or remote. Running LM Studio? Start its server and paste http://localhost:1234/v1. For a hosted gateway, or a provider offering an OpenAI-compatible API, paste its https base URL instead. vLLM, LocalAI and llama.cpp's server work the same way.
compatible.endpointHint: LM Studio uses http://localhost:1234/v1. A bare host and port gets /v1 appended, and defaults to https unless it is a local address.
compatible.apiKeyHint: Local servers usually ignore this and it can be left empty. Remote endpoints almost always require it.
compatible.modelPlaceholder: Click Fetch models, or type the id
compatible.modelHint: The model id comes from the server, so there is no default to fall back on.
compatible.noModels: The endpoint replied, but listed no models. Load a model in the server first.
compatible.remoteNeedsKey: This looks like a remote endpoint but no API key is set — most remote endpoints will reject the request.
compatible.insecureRemote: This remote endpoint uses plain http, so the API key and your code travel unencrypted. Prefer https.

settings.modelHint: Leave empty to use the default. Any model id works.

list.title: Engineering Practice
list.entryHint: Algorithm problems train implementation. Engineering projects train judgement through contracts, multi-file changes and acceptance results.
list.heading: Build a system one layer at a time
list.subtitle: Each project starts with a runnable skeleton. Stages check results, concurrency, latency and failure handling. Clear the current acceptance specs to unlock the next layer.

stage.locked: Clear the previous stage to unlock
stage.pitfallsHint: These approaches may pass a few specs, then fail at the boundaries
stage.revealBody: This shows the complete implementation for the stage. Read the failing specs and hints first, then decide whether to open it.

workspace.languageHint: Switching swaps the starter files and specs; each language keeps its own drafts

metrics.timelineHint: Virtual time on the x-axis, in-flight requests on the y-axis, a sequential implementation is a flat line at 1.

generator.title: Generate a project
generator.heading: Generate an engineering project
generator.subtitle: Describe the system and the technical decisions you want to practise. AI generates stages, workspace files, acceptance specs and a reference implementation.
generator.requestLabel: What do you want to practise
generator.requestHint: Name the system, then add the concerns you want tested, such as concurrency, caching, resilience or module boundaries.
generator.placeholder: e.g. a log batching uploader with backpressure, batching and drop policy
generator.verifyNote: The platform runs the reference solution to verify the generated project before saving it
generator.loadingHint: Designing stages, writing specs and running the reference implementation. The project is saved only after verification, which usually takes 1 to 3 minutes.
generator.problemsTitle: Problems found while executing this project
generator.noDiscrimination: the starter skeleton also passes, specs lack discrimination
generator.repairing: Verification failed, asking for a fix…

trace.note: Recorded across the whole acceptance run. Steps carry the file they came from, so the view follows execution across files.
